lane:
خُشَارٌ (K) and ↓خُشَارَةٌ (S, A, K) The bad part or parts [or the refuse] (Lh, S, K) of goods, or commodities, (Lh,) or of anything. (S, K.) And the latter, The worst kind, syn. شِيص, of lates. (A.) === What contains no لُبّ [or heart], of barley. (A, K.) === And the latter, The refuse of food remaining upon a table; that in which is no good. (S, A, K. *) === Also the latter, (S, A, K,) and the former, (K,) and ↓خُشَّارٌ, (IAar,) ‡ The refuse, or lowest or basest or meanest sort, of mankind, or of people; (IAar, S, A, K;) as also ↓خَاشِرٌ, accord. to the K, but correctly ↓خَاشِرَةٌ, as related by AA from IAar. (TA.) El-Hotei-ah says,

وَبَاعَ بَنِيهِ بَعْضُهُمْ بِخُشَارَةً

وَبِعْتَ لِذُبْيَانَ العَلَآءَ بِمَالِكِ

[And some of them have sold their sons for the refuse of mankind; but] thou hast purchased eminence for Dhubyán with Málik: in the S we find بِمَالِكَا [with thy property]: but it is correctly as above: Málik was a son of 'Oyeyneh Ibn- Hisn: the Benoo-'Ámir slew him: wherefore 'Oyeyneh made war upon them, and obtained his blood-revenge, and spoil: and to this event El- Hotei-ah refers in the verse above. (IB, TA.) خُشَّارٌ : see the paragraph next preceding.

entries.text: الخشار والخشارة، بضمهما: الرديء من كل شيء، وسفلة الناس، كالخاشر، وما لا لب له من الشعير. وخشر  يخشر: أبقى على المائدة الخشارة، و الشيء: نقى عنه خشارته، ضد، وشره. وكفرح: هرب جبنا. وخشاورة، بالضم: سكة بنيسابور. وذو خشران، بالفتح: من ألهان بن مالك.
